author: Carol Yang,Cao Jiaxuan
description:
As Beijing and Moscow double down on the Arctic shipping route, Europe is hitting the brakes.
Despite being the main destination for goods along the route and accounting for most of the world’s shipping giants, Europe opposes the commercialisation of Arctic transits, wary of fragile polar ecosystems and navigational risks amid rising anxiety over Russia and China’s closer polar collaboration.
“In Europe, cooperation between China and Russia on container shipping is often viewed as another...
title: Why the EU is giving Arctic shipping the cold shoulder as China and Russia push ahead

author: Ling Xin
description:
Chinese researchers have found a way to extract uranium from seawater at several times the target rate set by the US Department of Energy, putting China at the forefront of a global quest to tap into a vast source of nuclear fuel.
The team from the Chinese Academy of Sciences in Qingdao did this using a material they developed called PhosCage – a sponge-like molecular structure filled with phosphate groups that act as chemical traps.
In a statement, the researchers said they had recovered up to...
title: Chinese team extracts uranium from seawater at 8 times the US target rate

author: Albee Zhang
description:
The West African country of Burkina Faso has tested what observers say is a Chinese Sky Dragon 30 surface-to-air missile, in the latest sign that Chinese military equipment manufacturers are making inroads into the central Sahel state.
In footage released by the Burkinabe president’s office on Tuesday, multiple missiles were fired from a mobile launch vehicle. A matching search radar vehicle also appeared in the video.
The footage is part of a documentary series marking the fourth anniversary in...
title: In Burkina Faso, Sky Dragon 30 missiles point to China’s military export inroads

author: Albee Zhang
description:
China and the US have ended a two-year break in command-level contact with a meeting in Canada between the top PLA officer overseeing the Taiwan Strait and his US Pacific counterpart.
Chinese General Yang Zhibin, commander of the Eastern Theatre Command, and US Admiral Samuel Paparo met for the first time at the Indo-Pacific Chiefs of Defence Conference in Victoria, British Columbia, on Monday.
The US command said on Friday that Yang and Paparo discussed the importance of maintaining open lines...
title: China, US military commanders snap 2-year break with talks in Canada

author: Orange Wang
description:
China and South Korea have exchanged formal protests over the highly sensitive Taiwan question and Korean unity.
The two countries have been trying to improve relations in recent months, but South Korea’s national security adviser Wi Sung-lac said he had issued “a serious objection” after an official Chinese statement welcomed moves “towards the peaceful coexistence of the two states of South and North Korea”.
Meanwhile, Beijing “lodged serious representations” with Seoul over an art event that...
title: China and South Korea accuse each other of undermining key principles

author: Liu Zhen
description:
China sent armed trainer jets to drive away Philippine light aircraft over the disputed Scarborough Shoal on Wednesday, in a potentially more cost-effective tactic for its increasingly frequent air confrontations over the South China Sea.
At least three JL-10 trainers carrying PL-5 air-to-air missiles were involved in the incident over the shoal, according to a video clip posted to social media by the People’s Liberation Army Southern Theatre Command.
The footage showed the Chinese jet’s...
title: Chinese armed trainer jets drive away Philippine aircraft over Scarborough Shoal

author: Laura Zhou
description:
Cross-border disasters along China’s frontiers are putting Beijing’s neighbourhood diplomacy to the test as climate shocks grow and expose strategic vulnerabilities.
The stakes were highlighted last week after a sudden glacial collapse in the Himalayas unleashed a torrent of mud and flooding that ravaged nearby villages and the Gyirong Port between China and Nepal, leaving more than 1,250 dead in Nepal and 21 dead in the Tibet autonomous region. Thousands also remain missing.
Beyond the...
title: How natural disasters are putting China’s neighbourhood diplomacy to the test

author: Gaurav Kumar
description:
When Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping met at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, the encounter was short and carefully choreographed while the message was warm. Modi had earlier said that stable and predictable ties between the two largest nations on Earth matter for a multipolar Asia and world.
The larger moment will come on September 12 and 13, when Xi is expected to visit New Delhi for the first time in seven years. He is...
title: Despite rivalry, China-India coexistence is not a pipe dream

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
Fifty-two Singaporeans have been arrested and detained in China’s Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region following a law enforcement operation targeting suspected pyramid scheme activities and related offences, according to Singaporean authorities.
Singapore’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Singapore Police Force revealed the arrests in a joint statement on Friday, noting that Chinese authorities were still investigating the cases.
Sim Ann, Singapore’s second minister for foreign affairs, said...
title: China arrests 52 Singaporeans in Guangxi pyramid scheme crackdown

author: Chao Kong
description:
The enduring mystery of how the ancient Egyptians built the Great Pyramid of Giza – with its 2.3 million multi-tonne stone blocks – has puzzled researchers for centuries.
Mainstream archaeology holds that the pyramids were constructed from natural limestone or granite blocks precisely cut and hauled into place.
An alternative scientific theory suggests the blocks might have been cast from an early form of concrete, but that idea has long faced a critical question: how could such an artificial...
title: Could Roman concrete have clues on how Pyramid of Giza was built – and saved?

author: Nayan Seth
description:
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said both Washington and Beijing were seeking stability in their relationship and that he remained optimistic about ties ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s expected visit to the United States later this month.
“I am optimistic. The Chinese very much want to have a stable relationship. That’s the word they use: stability. We’re in favour of that as well,” Greer said in an interview with Fox News on Thursday.
He also said announcements on...
title: Trade chief Greer ‘optimistic’ the US and China can stabilise ties

author: SCMP
description:
We have selected seven stories from this week’s news across Hong Kong, mainland China, the wider Asia region and beyond that resonated with our readers and shed light on topical issues. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. Xi, Trump and Putin may hold trilateral meeting at next Apec forum, Kremlin says
A senior Russian aide suggested on Tuesday that Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin could hold a...
title: China’s Xi eyes Apec trilateral; no outrunning deadly Nepal floods: SCMP’s 7 highlights

author: Zhang Tong,Victoria Bela
description:
Even as China installs new solar and wind power capacity faster than the rest of the world combined, it is setting new benchmarks for the technologies through innovation.
This year alone, Chinese companies and researchers have generated the first electricity from high-altitude winds 4,000 metres above Earth, cleared the last hurdle to commercialising a cheaper and more efficient alternative to silicon solar panels, begun trials of the world’s most powerful floating and fixed-bottom offshore wind...
title: China’s solar, wind innovations amid rapid green power buildout

author: Dulue Mbachu
description:
The latest US visa restrictions on citizens of African countries are facing increasing criticism that they are not only punitive but also likely to backfire by driving those nations closer to China.
Since August 1, visa services have been suspended in 25 African cities, forcing applicants to travel to other approved locations, sometimes in another country.
Travellers from 30 African nations must also post a US$20,000 bond, which is refundable if they depart on time.
Separately, 26 countries face...
title: China stands to gain from US visa restrictions targeting African countries

author: Frank Wilczek
description:
Cats are wonderful gymnasts. Their ability to land on their feet – even when dropped upside-down – caught the attention of two of the nineteenth century’s greatest mathematical physicists, Sir George Gabriel Stokes and James Clerk Maxwell.
The remarkable feats of cats inspired these theorists to perform, in the 1850s, legendary experiments in “cat-turning”, as Maxwell later described:
“There is a tradition in Trinity that when I was here I discovered a method of throwing a cat so as not to light...
title: Cats and mind-full mechanics: what happens when quantum physics meets the brain
